cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, written for the choirmaster, and he's talking straight to the LORD. He opens with, "O LORD, You have searched me and known me." Friend, I got searched every single time somebody dug through my junk drawer looking for tape, but NOBODY ever knew me.

cards.question: David says the LORD knows when he sits down and when he gets up. What else does the LORD understand from afar?

cards.text: The LORD searches out David's path and his lying down, and He's aware of ALL his ways. ALL of them, friend, and some days I'm not even aware of all MY ways.

cards.question: David says the LORD only knows his words after he says them out loud.

cards.text: Then David says the LORD hems him in behind and before, and has laid His hand on him. Behind AND before, friend, so David can't even back out of this one.

cards.question: The LORD knows David inside and out. David says knowledge like that is too ___ for him to reach.

cards.text: Then David asks two questions: "Where can I go to escape Your Spirit? Where can I flee from Your presence?" Buckle up, friend, because he's about to picture every hiding spot there is.

cards.question: David says that if he went up to the heavens or made his bed in Sheol, the LORD would be there too.

cards.text: Next he pictures rising on the wings of the dawn, or settling by the farthest sea. That's the "new phone number, no forwarding address" plan, friend. Every adult has thought about it at least once.

cards.question: Even by the farthest sea, David says the LORD's hand will ___ him.

cards.text: Last idea: what if David says the darkness will surely hide him, and the light around him will become night? Friend, I spent YEARS in the dark at the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know a good hiding spot when I see one.

cards.question: Why can't the darkness hide David from God?

answers.text: Night is as bright as day to God
God simply waits for the morning
David's voice always gives him away

cards.question: The heavens, Sheol, the farthest sea, the dark. What's David's point in naming all these places?

answers.text: There's nowhere God isn't with him
Some places are too far for God
God only follows when he calls

cards.text: Now David goes back before he was even born: the LORD formed his inmost being and knit him together in his mother's womb. KNIT him, friend, and I still need three tries to tie my own apron.

cards.question: Thinking about how God made him, what does David do?

cards.text: David says he is fearfully and wonderfully made, and he knows very well that God's works are marvelous. Friend, I once sold for 25 cents out of a clearance bin, and even I'm feeling that one.

cards.question: David was made in secret, woven together in the depths of the earth. He says his frame was hidden from God while he was being made.

cards.text: And God's eyes saw David's body while it was still unformed. That's seeing the cookie before the dough's even mixed.

cards.question: David says all his days were written in God's book only after he lived them.

cards.text: I think David is in awe here. He tells God that His thoughts are precious to him.

cards.question: David says that if he tried to count God's thoughts, they would outnumber the grains of sand. What's he saying about God's thoughts?

answers.text: There are too many to count
They change from day to day

cards.text: Then David says, "when I awake, I am still with You." Most mornings I wake up to the snooze button, but David wakes up still with God.
Then the psalm takes a hard turn. David turns his attention to the wicked.

cards.question: As the psalm takes a hard turn, what does David ask God to do to the wicked?
David tells the bloodthirsty men to get away from him. He says they speak of God with honest words.

cards.text: David asks, "Do I not hate those who hate You, O LORD, and detest those who rise against You?" Then he says he hates them with perfect hatred and counts them as his enemies.

Then David circles back to how this psalm opened, and now he's ASKING for it: "Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my concerns." Friend, most of us dodge the checkup. David is BOOKING one.

cards.question: As God searches him, David asks God to see if there's any ___ way in him.
David's last request is to be led somewhere. Where?

answers.text: In the way that lasts forever
In the way of his fathers
In the way back to Jerusalem

findings.problem: Calling David "king of Israel" is a Bible fact from outside Psalm 139. The card cites only Psalm 139:1, which identifies this as a psalm of David but does not support his kingship, so the outside fact lacks its own reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The earlier cards do not give the baker a way to infer "wonderful" rather than "heavy" or "painful" as David's response to being completely known. This simply blanks the psalm's unseen wording, leaving the baker to guess or already know verse 6.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup establishes only that David pictures himself by the farthest sea. It does not establish what God's hand will do there, and God's presence alone does not distinguish "guide" from "warn." The blank therefore tests the unseen wording of verse 10 rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The preceding card sets up David's request to be searched and tested, but it does not establish the particular kind of way he asks God to find. "Offensive" is supplied only by the unseen wording of verse 24, making this a wording cloze rather than an inference from the setup.
